# Jubilees Chapter 35 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Rebekah's testament; the reconciliation of Esau and Jacob; Rebekah's death

---

**35:1** In the first year of the seventh week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Rebekah called her son Jacob and gave him instructions regarding his brother Esau, saying:

**35:2** "I have been watching and observing all the deeds of your brother Esau, my son, and I know that his deeds are evil and full of wickedness. He pays no attention to the commands of his father or his mother.

**35:3** But you, my son — guard your soul and conduct yourself uprightly in everything, and you will find favor before God and before men.

**35:4** Watch out for Esau, so that he does not rise up against you and there is no quarrel between you; for the shedding of a brother's blood would be an abomination before God.

**35:5** Know this, my son: all the children of Belial will rise up against Israel and against all the nations.

**35:6** I am anxious about all of your brother Esau's deeds, lest he harm you and you perish. Be watchful of him and cautious; but do not seek his destruction.

**35:7** Know that from the time I saw you in the womb I loved you with all my heart and soul. I have loved you more than any of my other children, for you are truly my beloved son."

**35:8** Rebekah wept bitterly, and Jacob wept as well.

**35:9** Rebekah said: "O LORD God, let me not see the day when my son Jacob dies before me, for that would grieve my heart and soul exceedingly."

**35:10** She sent and called Esau and said to him: "I have something to say to you, my son." He came to her.

**35:11** She said: "I have a request, my son; will you listen to my voice?"

**35:12** Esau said: "I will listen, my mother." She said: "I am asking you, my son — I entreat you: honor your brother Jacob and love him.

**35:13** I love both of you; but my particular request is this: do not harm or hurt him all the days of your life and as long as you live. I could not endure being his enemy."

**35:14** Esau said: "I will do as you say. I will not harm my brother Jacob. I am reconciled to him, and I love him more than my own soul."

**35:15** She said: "Bless the LORD your God who has given you this spirit of reconciliation. You have sworn before the LORD not to harm your brother Jacob. Now swear to me by God that you will keep this word."

**35:16** Esau swore to Rebekah by God that he would not harm Jacob for the whole of his life.

**35:17** Rebekah called Jacob and told him that Esau had been reconciled to him and had sworn before God. She rejoiced greatly.

**35:18** Then Rebekah fell ill and died, and Jacob and Esau mourned her deeply.

**35:19** She was buried in the cave of Machpelah at Mamre with her husband Isaac. All her sons and Jacob's sons buried her with great weeping and mourning.

**35:20** In the second year of the first week of the forty-sixth jubilee, Isaac died. His sons Jacob and Esau buried him.

**35:21** Esau departed to Edom, and Jacob dwelt at Hebron. Whenever Esau's household lacked, Jacob sent them food.

**35:22** Whenever Esau passed by, he sent gifts and greetings to Jacob. Peace prevailed between them throughout all the days of Isaac and Rebekah.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus following LOGOS. Rebekah's testament is unique to Jubilees and is an important text for understanding the book's theology of brotherly reconciliation. "Children of Belial" (v.5) is a Second Temple designation for wicked opponents. The portrait of Rebekah as a peace-broker is distinctive and humanizing.*
